title: SPEAK INTO THE NEW WEEK BEFORE THE ENEMY DOES
text: Stop. Before you scroll past this, before you let another sentence of this week be written by anything other than your own mouth, I need you to sit up straight and pay attention because there is a race happening right now that most believers don't even know they are running. [music] Somewhere in the unseen realm, two voices are competing for the right to define the next seven days of your life. And whichever voice speaks first is the voice that sets the terms. I am not exaggerating when I say this. The person who speaks first over a week doesn't just make a suggestion. They file a claim. And if you are silent, if you scroll into Monday morning without opening your mouth, somebody else's claim gets processed by default. And that somebody is really kind to you. I feel a specific urgency in my spirit as I say this. This is not a generic exhaltation to have a good attitude about the week ahead. This is a summons. There is a new week standing at the door of your life right now. Unclaimed. Unclaimed. Unclaimed. And the enemy has never once in history waited politely for you to get around to praying about it. He speaks early. He speaks first. He whispers Sunday night while you're still full from dinner, half asleep, guard down. And by the time you officially start your week on Monday morning, he has already filed several claims you never contested. Not this week. Not while I'm standing here. Not while you're reading this with a heartbeat still in your chest and breath still in your lungs. We are going to speak fast. We are going to speak loud. We're going to speak now. Before there was light, before there was a single visible thing in existence, there was speech, not silence, waiting for circumstances to develop on their own. Not passive hope that things would eventually turn out fine. Speech. God did not look at the darkness and think about it. He spoke into it. And the void which had no shape, no direction, no defined future was given form the moment a voice entered it. This is the pattern for everything that has ever come into structured existence. The void exists first and then a voice enters it and whatever voice enters first begins to shape what emerges. Your week right now before Monday has even fully arrived is a void. It has no defined shape yet in the sense that matters. Yes, there are appointments on your calendar. Yes, there are tasks assigned. Yes, there are things you already know are coming. But the atmosphere of the week, whether it moves in fear or faith, whether it moves in delay or breakthrough, whether it moves in conflict or peace, that atmosphere has not yet been permanently set. It is still void, still waiting for a voice. And the question this morning is simply, whose voice is going to enter first? Say it with me. I speak into this week before the enemy does not as a hopeful wish but as an act of spiritual authority. Let the fire of first speech fall. Dares column fire of the beginning word. Let my voice enter every void of this week before any other voice can. [music] I want to establish something further because I don't want this to just sound poetic. [music] I want you to understand the mechanics of what we're doing. Job 22:28 says, "Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee, and the light shall shine upon thy ways." That word decree is a legal term. It's not a hopeful suggestion offered up into the air. A decree is a binding pronouncement. And when it comes from a position of covenant authority, it gets established. Meaning it becomes fixed, settled, structurally embedded into the unfolding of events. This is not magic. This is not positive thinking. This is a covenant right given to those who walk with God. And most believers have never exercised it because nobody ever told them it was theirs to exercise. This morning, before anything happens, before a single meeting starts, before a single phone rings with news you weren't expecting, I want you to decree. I decree that this week is a week where delay is exposed and defeated before it can even fully form. Let every decree lock into place immediately. Chhatam dab shalem. Fire of the immediate seal. In Numbers chapter 13, 12 spies were sent to search out the promised land, and 10 of them came back and spoke first, and what they spoke was fear. They said the land was good, but the people were giants, and the spies felt like grasshoppers in their own sight. That report went out into the camp before Caleb and Joshua could establish a counternarrative. And [music] by the time the minority report of faith tried to speak, the majority report of fear had already infected an entire generation. Numbers 14 tells us that entire generation died in the wilderness. Not because God changed his mind about the promised land, but because the wrong voice got there first and shaped the atmosphere of unbelief that everyone else absorbed. I want you to feel the weight of that. It was not that the promise was cancelled. This is exactly what happens when we allow Sunday night anxiety or a discouraging conversation or a negative headline or an old memory of past failure to speak first into our week. It's not that God's promise over your week has been cancelled.
